item.title: Geneva (NY) FD Receives State Grant to Replace 2006 Pumper
item.description: The Geneva (NY) Fire Department has been awarded $1 million to replace a 2006 engine that has exceeded its service life. item.title: Petaluma (CA)’s Aging Fire Station 1 Slated for $8.7M Renovation
item.description: Petaluma, California's downtown fire station will undergo renovations starting this winter, including seismic upgrades, hazardous material abatement, and improved accessibility, with completion expected by early 2027. The post Petaluma (CA)’s Aging Fire Station 1 Slated for $8.7M Renovation appeared first on Fire Apparatus: Fire trucks, fire engines, emergency vehicles, and firefighting equipment.

item.title: FAMA Forum: Supporting and Advancing the Industry
item.description: Jason Witmier, the new FAMA president for 2026, emphasizes the importance of teamwork and gradual change in the fire apparatus industry, highlighting challenges in navigating information and opinions. The post FAMA Forum: Supporting and Advancing the Industry appeared first on Fire Apparatus: Fire trucks, fire engines, emergency vehicles, and firefighting equipment.

item.title: Plainfield Township (MI) FD Welcomes New Engine
item.description: The new Engine 3 has a 1,750-gallon-per-minute (gpm) pump and a 500-gallon water tank. It's also equipped to respond to vehicle crashes, medical emergencies, and smaller-scale hazardous materials incidents. The post Plainfield Township (MI) FD Welcomes New Engine appeared first on Fire Apparatus: Fire trucks, fire engines, emergency vehicles, and firefighting equipment.

item.title: CA Fire Apparatus Crashes En Route to Separate Collision
item.description: A Sonoma County fire engine crashed while responding to another collision in Windsor. Two people in a Prius were hospitalized; no firefighters were injured. The incident is under investigation. The post CA Fire Apparatus Crashes En Route to Separate Collision appeared first on Fire Apparatus: Fire trucks, fire engines, emergency vehicles, and firefighting equipment.

item.title: City Apparatus Taken from Yantic (CT) Engine Company Back in Service
item.description: Norwich's Yantic Fire Engine Co. No. 1 was shut down for non-compliance with a new unified command policy, leading to repossession of firetrucks. City officials assert the policy enhances public safety. The post City Apparatus Taken from Yantic (CT) Engine Company Back in Service appeared first on Fire Apparatus: Fire trucks, fire engines, emergency vehicles, and firefighting equipment.

item.title: Staten Island (NY) Reinforced: $9M to Modernize Firehouses, Train Next Generation of First Responders
item.description: Staten Island officials announced $9 million in federal funding to modernize firehouses and build an EMS training center, improving response times and service for local communities. item.title: Morgan (AL) County Commission Districts Donating $40,000 to Somerville Volunteer Fire Dept.
item.description: The Morgan County Commission is donating $40,000 for repairs to the Somerville Volunteer Fire Department's parking lot, funded from road and bridge funds to expedite necessary improvements. item.title: Mold Found in 20 of 22 Witchita (KS) Fire Stations; One Evacuated, Vice Mayor Says
item.description: Mold was found in 20 of Wichita's 22 fire stations, leading to the evacuation of Station 15. Officials cite deferred maintenance as a cause, impacting emergency response times. item.title: Orangeburg (SC) to Replace Apparatus
item.description: Orangeburg City Council approved financing for a new fire truck costing up to $945,630 to replace an outdated model, with annual debt payments of about $90,000 over ten years.
